claims.claim: For every fixed threshold τ≥2, a simple three-occurrence color sequence encodes a spanning forest with exactly two roots, even root degrees, and odd nonroot degrees.
claims.evidence: Let N=2n and use n−1 colors. Since 0<τ−1<τ and 2(τ−1)≥τ, adjacent placement of a color's first two stacks would eliminate them and leave its sole remaining stack unremovable. Thus an emptying play has N−2 distinct occupied vertices after phase one. Each last occurrence must be placed at an empty vertex adjacent to both earlier occurrences: adjacency to zero or one leaves an unremovable stack. Directing two edges from that center to the cleared vertices gives every initially occupied vertex exactly one parent and the two initially empty vertices none. A nonroot center was cleared strictly before its children, so parent chains strictly decrease clearing time and cannot cycle. The N−2 distinct edges therefore form two rooted trees. Every use of a center adds two children, making root degrees even and nonroot degrees one plus an even number, hence odd.
claims.search_method: Direct symbolic case analysis of all possible matching-neighbor counts, followed by a clearing-time invariant and supplemental exact finite state-space checks.

claims.claim: For the leaf-corona G of a connected subcubic graph H, the above prefix can empty G if and only if H has a Hamiltonian path.
claims.evidence: For |V(H)|=1 both sides hold. Otherwise, a pendant root in the parity forest has degree zero, while a nonroot pendant has degree one. Two pendant roots would already be two isolated components; no pendant root would leave, after deleting leaf edges, two components of H each with exactly one odd-degree vertex, contradicting handshaking. Hence exactly one root is a pendant a′ and is isolated, while the other root r is original. Removing pendant vertices leaves a spanning tree T of H. If r=a, all degrees in T are even, impossible for a nontrivial tree. Otherwise precisely a and r have odd degree. Subcubicity makes every other tree degree exactly two, and the degree sum forces deg_T(a)=deg_T(r)=1, so T is a spanning path. Conversely, from a Hamiltonian path v₁,…,vₙ, leave v₁′ and vₙ empty, place each initial pair on v_{n−i+1}′ and v_{n−i}, and use v_{n−i+1} as its later center. The paired vertices are nonadjacent and each center is empty when used, so the prefix empties G.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive root-location and parity analysis, verification of the converse placement indices, exhaustive parity-forest comparison on all 516 labeled connected subcubic graphs through five vertices, and direct game-state search through four vertices at thresholds 2, 3, and 5.

claims.claim: Fitting Hexasort is NP-hard for every exact fixed threshold τ≥2, even on graphs of maximum degree four.
claims.evidence: Reducing from Hamiltonian Path on connected subcubic graphs is polynomial. The leaf-corona raises each original degree by one, so its maximum degree is at most four, and Claim 1 gives the required equivalence for the prefix. Appending N one-off colors of height one is a valid Fitting conversion: at τ≥2 they never vanish, so a configuration with k occupied vertices accepts exactly N−k of the N suffix stacks. Hence the whole suffix fits iff k=0, i.e. iff the prefix emptied the graph. The sequence has linear length and uses only heights τ−1 and 1, so the construction works for every exact fixed τ≥2.
claims.search_method: Checked both reduction directions, graph degree, construction size, threshold arithmetic, and the exact suffix-capacity identity; supplemented by exact constructive simulations.

claims.claim: Complete classification: the constant-threshold problem is NP-complete for every fixed τ≥2, while τ=1 is trivial.
claims.evidence: Claim 2 supplies NP-hardness. Membership in NP follows from a certificate listing one selected vertex per explicitly listed stack; legality and all same-color height sums can be simulated in polynomial time. Thus every exact fixed τ≥2 case is NP-complete. For every fixed upper bound T≥2, the exact-t=2 reduction is also a reduction into the restriction t≤T, while membership in NP remains unchanged. At τ=1 every positive-height placement immediately vanishes, so every sequence fits on a nonempty graph; on an empty graph only the empty sequence fits. These cases exhaust the positive thresholds allowed by the model.
claims.search_method: Independently checked NP verification, exact-threshold and bounded-threshold quantifiers, and the τ=1 empty-graph boundary case.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for a complexity classification of Fitting Hexasort when t is bounded by a fixed constant. The draft proves NP-completeness for every exact fixed τ≥2, also explicitly derives NP-completeness for every fixed promise bound t≤T with T≥2, and handles the only remaining positive threshold T=1 as trivial. The reduction establishes the requested hardness at stronger maximum-degree-four and constant-height restrictions, while NP membership completes the classification. Therefore the entire target is resolved at the requested strength, and the draft's claimed FULL resolution is accurate.
